speech
Phonosemantic compound. 言 represents the meaning and 隹 represents the sound.
何也。从言隹聲。

Phono-semantic compound (形聲 /形声, OC *djul): semantic 言 (“speak”) + phonetic 隹 (OC *tjul).
From *du + *-i (“suffix in independent pronouns”); cognate with 疇 (OC *du, “who”), 孰 (OC *djɯwɢ, “which one; who”) (Schuessler, 2007). In other Sino-Tibetan languages, compare Mizo tû (“who; which”), Chepang दोह् (“what”), Proto-Kuki-Chin *tuu (“who; which (relativizer)”) (Schuessler, 2007; STEDT).
Contraction of 啥人 (siáⁿ-lâng).
Contraction of 底人 (tī-lâng).
Contraction of 是誰／是谁 (chī-chūi).
From shortening of 是誰／是谁 (chī-choa̍h), from 是誰仔／是谁仔 (chī-chūi-á).

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: 形義通解; 金文字形; 《說文》欄
evidence.text: The entry reports bronze forms with 言 plus phonetic 隹; it interprets the original sense as a dark/black horse and cites a bronze inscription where the 言 component is slightly distorted and the graph is read as 騅. It separately reports a Zhongshan bronze use of 隹 in 其隹能之, read as 其誰能之, suggesting 隹 was used for 誰 before 言 was added. Its seal-script and manuscript entries are shown, while no oracle-bone form is listed. The page also quotes 說文: 誰，何也。从言，隹聲。
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「誰」

evidence.source: 中華民國教育部《異體字字典》
evidence.text: The dictionary records 誰 as 說文's ‘何也。从言，隹聲’ and gives modern Mandarin shéi and shuí as pronunciation and literary reading. It documents the interrogative-person use with 孟子·公孫丑下, ‘當今之世，舍我其誰也’; it also records ‘anyone’/assertive use and rhetorical ‘難道’, with examples from 元史、紅樓夢 and 漢書 respectively. The online entry does not date the cited passages or establish a chronological semantic sequence.
evidence.title: 教育部《異體字字典》：誰

evidence.text: The page quotes 說文's ‘何也。从言隹聲’ and supplies the gloss ‘who’, with old-Chinese reconstruction *djul attributed to Zhengzhang. This is a secondary summary, not independent paleographic confirmation; its reconstruction should not be conflated with Baxter–Sagart.
evidence.title: 誰 - 维基词典

evidence.field: Glyph origin; phonetic-series table; Mandarin pronunciation
evidence.text: The opened page labels 誰 a phonosemantic compound: semantic 言 and phonetic 隹, giving Zhengzhang (2003) OC *djul for 誰 and *tjul for 隹; the table lists related phonetic-series members including 騅. It reports Mandarin shéi/shuí. These are the page's secondary-source assertions. The supplied local Baxter–Sagart row instead gives 誰 MC dzywij and OC *[d]uj, so the two reconstruction systems differ and should remain separately attributed. The local Unihan kMandarin rows are 誰 shuí shéi and 谁 shéi; no local row for 隹 was supplied, so no modern Unihan reading for the phonetic component is asserted here.
evidence.title: 誰 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.field: 字形; 《說文》; 形義通解
evidence.text: The entry lists one small-seal example and four bronze examples, no oracle-bone example, and six manuscript examples. It quotes 說文: 誰，何也。从言，隹聲. Its own analysis says the bronze graph combines 言 with phonetic 隹, and proposes an original ‘dark horse’ sense, identifying a bronze graph with a distorted 言 component as 騅. It also reports a Zhongshan king bronze inscription reading 其隹能之 as 其誰能之, and infers that 隹 was used for 誰 before 言 was added. These are the entry’s paleographic interpretations; it does not give artifact dates or independently establish the horse name’s pronunciation.

evidence.source: 中華民國教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.text: The entry quotes 說文’s analysis 从言，隹聲 and gloss 何也. It gives modern Mandarin shéi and shuí, records the interrogative-person use with 孟子·公孫丑下, and also lists ‘anyone’ and rhetorical ‘難道’ uses with examples from 元史、紅樓夢 and 漢書. The entry supplies no dates for those cited passages and does not establish a chronological sequence among these senses.

editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

search_audit.outcome: Opened the Ministry of Education 誰 entry and the Palace Museum inscription article. Official Unihan record URLs for 誰 and 隹 were attempted but inaccessible. Search results support the Zhongshan inscription reading, but do not resolve the proposed horse-name pronunciation.

gaps: Earliest dated use of 誰 as an interrogative pronoun was not established. The sources inspected quote the received 說文 gloss and later classical examples but do not date the earliest surviving inscription or textual witness.

CUHK interprets bronze 誰 as originally ‘dark horse’ (騅) and reports a bronze use of bare 隹 for the interrogative 誰. These claims suggest graphic/sense history, but the inspected material does not independently establish how the horse-name was pronounced or prove a sound-based borrowing from that name. Do not treat the reconstruction of the pronoun alone as evidence for the horse's name pronunciation.

No oracle-bone form is listed by the inspected CUHK entry; absence from that entry does not prove the graph was absent from all oracle-bone material. The exact dates and provenance of the cited bronze artifacts were not verified.

The semantic path from the reported horse sense to the interrogative pronoun, and the relative chronology of the bare 隹 and 言+隹 uses, need primary inscription editions or specialist paleographic discussion beyond the inspected page.

The simplified counterpart relation 誰 → 谁 is present in the dossier's imported record, but the inspected sources here did not provide an explicit source statement establishing this standardization; component-level origin classification should therefore remain uncertain absent a supporting citation. The visible 言-side shorthand 讠 is not separately evidenced in the opened sources.

The official Unicode Unihan character records could not be accessed through the web tool. Local supplied rows report the readings, but are local data, not verified external pages; no supplied local row gives 隹's reading.
No exact local Baxter–Sagart row for 隹 was supplied. Consequently, the provided local table permits reporting 誰's MC dzywij and OC *[d]uj, but not a same-system host-versus-component comparison.

The CUHK site is repeatedly useful across character research, but no reuse license for its character-specific entries or bulk text was verified. Recommend citation and paraphrase only, not a tracked extract.
The earliest dated attestation of 誰 as an interrogative pronoun was not established. The inspected sources quote 說文 and cite later received texts, but no dated earliest witness was verified.

The CUHK entry proposes that the bronze graph 誰 first meant a dark horse and says a bronze inscription form is read as 騅. The horse-name’s original pronunciation was not independently established here. A reconstruction for the pronoun alone does not demonstrate the name or pronunciation of the horse, so the proposed relation must not be presented as a proven sound-based borrowing.

The reported Zhongshan bronze use of bare 隹 for 誰 supports a reading of that inscription, but the sources inspected do not settle whether it represents a whole graph used for the pronoun, the relative chronology of that use and 言+隹, or the semantic path from a proposed horse sense.

The CUHK 誰 entry lists no oracle-bone example. That is evidence about the entry’s coverage, not proof that no oracle-bone form exists. Exact artifact provenance and dates for the cited bronze forms were not verified.

The opened Ministry of Education entry presents 誰 and cites uses, but does not explicitly document the standardization relation 誰 → 谁 or the component simplification 言 → 讠. Treat the dossier’s simplification note as an imported assertion, not newly verified evidence.

The exact official Unicode Unihan records for 誰 and 隹 were inaccessible to the web tool. The supplied local 誰 row is shuí shéi; no supplied local 隹 row is available. No same-system Baxter–Sagart comparison between host and component is established by this packet.

No usable, character-specific historical glyph image with inspected identity and reuse provenance was established. Generic or unrelated Commons results cannot support an image choice; the Academia Sinica CC0 notice is general and does not substitute for an inspected 誰 query record. No glyph was visually inspected.
The repeatedly useful CUHK character page has no verified reuse license in the material inspected. Cite and paraphrase its entry; no local extract is recommended.

limitations.text: No character-specific historical glyph image is available here to illustrate the reported bronze forms or the bare 隹 reading for 誰; without a verified image, the graphic relationship cannot be shown directly.
